note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a EST 6; A06b EST 6; L05 EST 29): ordinary naturalisation after 8 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen keeps it on taking another (loss applies only to naturalised citizens, not modelled). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Estonia, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in Estonia for 8 years, of which the last 5 years permanently. ... Renunciation of citizenship of another country required. ... Person voluntarily acquires citizenship of another country. Provision is also applicable to persons who acquired citizenship during minority (exceptions outlined in EST 3 apply). Article 8 of the Constitution and Article 5(3) of the Citizenship Act, which preclude deprivation of Estonian citizenship obtained by birth.
